LESSON: BEEKEEPING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Animal Production
Topic 2.4: Beekeeping
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Beekeeping, part of Animal Production in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: How are bees reared?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Beekeeping together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
.

Core Competences to be developed:

● Digital literacy: learner search using digital devices information on how to stock a hive and harvest honey.

● Self-efficacy: learner develops self-confidence while role playing with peers on how to harvest honey.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety and security: learner simulates how to ensure own safety when harvesting honey.

● Health promotion issues: learner explains nutritional benefits of honey for health and also demonstrates how to remove bee

stings as a first aid measure.

● Socio-economic and environmental issues: learner learns aspects of animal welfare, for example feeding and watering to

ensure that bees are attracted and retained in the hives.

Suggested Learning Resources: Hives or hive models, bee handling equipment such as hive tool smoker with handle and

enhanced grip, bee suit, Adapted computers with appropriate accessibility features, Appropriate applications/ software,
